page.text:
A relation $R$ on $X$ is *antisymmetric* when cycles of length two can
only occur trivially:
$x \mathrel{R} y \land y \mathrel{R} x \implies x = y$. Antisymmetry
prohibits mutual preference between distinct elements, serving as the
defining non-symmetric property of orders.
